messages:
RaviK: Quick note — I'm seeing tiny token-level diffs when a long prompt is handed off across GPU shards during a streamed generation. Happens intermittently at chunk boundaries (~4096 multiples).
Clara: Can you paste the minimal repro? Which model and quantization?
RaviK: repro steps: 1) create prompt ~18k tokens with repeated sections, 2) stream generate with shard-size=4096, 3) compare tokens between single-shard reference and multi-shard handoff. Observed mismatch at offsets like 8191-8193.
RaviK: logs: ```kv_index=8191->wrap, write_len=2, prev_anchor=8190, applied_prefill=false```
Marta: That sounds like fragmentation in the KV handoff window, maybe we lost a sentinel while compacting the cache. I saw similar divergence when prefill writes race with window-compact on the receiver.
Luis: Did you run with int8 quantized runtime? We had an unrelated memcopy alignment bug show only on int8 builds.
RaviK: Ran both fp16 and int8. fp16 diverged more frequently, int8 less but still some occurrences. Sequence of steps seems tied to where we do prefix-eviction vs. shard-join.
Clara: Could you try adding an explicit kv-barrier (flush/ack) at the shard boundaries as a smoke check? If divergence disappears, that narrows it down.
RaviK: Will try. Quick patch: insert an ``ACK_KV_BOUNDARY`` before shard-join and skip immediate compact if ack missing. Triggering now on branch `ml/kv-frag-scan`.
eng_runtime_bot: CI triggered: ml/kv-frag-scan — shard-integration smoke matrix (gpu-2x) started. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/3352104567/artifacts
Marta: Another hypothesis — RoPE index scaling: when we replay tokens across a cross-shard boundary, index computation may shift if offsets are applied inconsistently. Check that the receiver applies the same global base index before interpolation.
RaviK: Good call. I dumped per-layer rot-sin/cos anchors pre/post-handoff and saw a one-off index shift in layer 10 on receiver. Patch incoming to carry absolute-base-index in the handoff header.
Luis: If that fixes it, we should add a regression in the long-context suite that fuzzes handoffs + random prefill/eviction interleavings. I've got a harness for that.
Clara: Agreed — add a small test that runs 50 handoff rounds with random prefill sizes and verifies token-perfect equality vs single-shard reference. Keep it lightweight so it can run nightly.
RaviK: CI finished — quick result: with ACK + absolute-base-index header, local smoke shows diff-rate -> 0/200 handoffs. Pushing PR now: https://git.internal/r/kv/frag-fix.
Marta: Awesome. After PR lands, let's run the full fuzz harness Luis mentioned. If it holds, we can backport to the 1.7.x maintenance branch.
RaviK: Will coordinate with eng-runtime for a canary rollout. Leaving notes in the PR about observable signals (kv-wrap-count, boundary-acks, rot-index-deltas).
Clara: Thanks — please ping when canary is up so SRE can watch latency regressions. :thumbsup:
RaviK: Will do.
